title: Invoicely — Developer API Keys
objective: You hold a read-only API key, documented as GET-only. Delete an invoice with it.

verifier.condition: An invoice is deleted using a key documented and issued as read-only.

weakness: The scope check decides whether a read-only key may call an endpoint by matching the request path against a list of "read endpoints" and never compares the HTTP method, so DELETE on a path that is normally read with GET is allowed through.
seededData: Three synthetic invoices and both a read-only and a full-access API key, shown on the developer page. In memory; reset with the instance.

credentials.label: Customer
credentials.note: Has both a read-only and a full-access API key on the developer page.

hints: List invoices and fetch a single one with the read-only key, then see which other HTTP methods that same address accepts.
A key's permission is often decided by which address is being called. Check whether the METHOD is decided the same way.
Send a DELETE to a single invoice's address using the read-only key.
burpNotes: Change only the HTTP method on an otherwise normal, successful read-only-key request.
